scope.reason: The rebuild tree src_new/ + tests_new/ is the product being cleaned, ahead of the src_new -> src cutover. The legacy src/ and tests/ trees are slated for deletion once the rebuild is fully working and are kept only for reference, so they are readable to explain why a rebuild module ports an odd behaviour, but are never swept and never filed against. docs/audits/ is sealed rather than referenced: it holds nine prior findings reports, and a sweeper that reads one has stopped being blind, which makes the pass compromised by definition. Both ledgers are sealed for the same reason. The governance artifacts (project description, requirements, user stories, architecture) are readable because activities 0 and 2 exist to compare the code against them. tmp/ is scratch and never a product.

0.title: Specs — requirements and user stories exist, are testable, and cover the code

passes.direction_note: Reconnaissance only — no source or test file was touched.
passes.note: Seed reconnaissance sweep — one subagent, briefed on the full flag catalogue and the whole scope, deliberately shallow and time-boxed. Returned 22 findings across 12 flag classes and reported no contamination. This is a sample, not an inventory: it satisfies no gate and makes no completeness claim. Its only purpose is to give every activity a non-empty denominator, so that activity 0's and 1.a's verification is not vacuous by construction. Findings carry the sweeper's own confidence rating and are unverified — each is checked under Phase 2.5 by the activity that owns it, before any fix.
